stories.title: Streamer HAchubby says she has cancer and is going to Korea for treatment
paragraphs: TalkEsport reports that Twitch streamer HAchubby disclosed a cancer diagnosis during a November 4 stream and is going to Korea for treatment.
The announcement drew more than 10,000 votes on a surfaced r/LivestreamFail discussion. That shows strong attention in one community, not a consensus about her health or treatment.

The saved reporting gives no further medical specifics. The update is a notable creator story, though the disclosure date places it in the seven-day window rather than the confirmed 24-hour news window.

scoreNotes.general: A widely discussed personal announcement from a gaming creator, reported by a gaming outlet and surfaced in substantial community discussion.
scoreNotes.heat: The r/LivestreamFail result showed more than 10,000 votes, indicating unusually strong attention in that community; this is not a measure of broader public sentiment.
scoreNotes.time: The report says HAchubby disclosed the diagnosis on November 4, within the preceding seven days, but the saved evidence does not establish that the disclosure fell inside this edition's 24-hour window.
scoreNotes.ethos: A news report and an indexed community post support that she made the announcement. The saved results do not establish a cancer type or further medical details.

stories.title: SNK’s Fatal Fury streamer cup brings 20 creators together on Nov. 7
paragraphs: SNK says 20 streamers and fighting-game personalities will take part in a Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves Streamer Cup on November 7.
The field includes VTubers, streamers, and professional players, making this a creator-led showcase around SNK’s current fighting game rather than a standard esports-only tournament.
The event is imminent, but the saved results do not establish its eventual audience or full broadcast details.

stories.title: Date Everything! passes one million copies sold
paragraphs: Sassy Chap Games announced that its dating sim Date Everything! has sold one million copies.
The milestone gives the small studio a measurable commercial result for its debut game. The saved announcement does not provide a platform split or explain how sales have changed over time.

stories.title: Phantom Blade Zero opens with four million sales in 72 hours
paragraphs: S-Game’s action game Phantom Blade Zero reportedly sold more than four million copies in its first 72 hours after launching October 29.

GamesRadar also reported a Steam peak of about 820,000 players. Alinea Analytics estimated roughly $223 million in combined Steam and PlayStation 5 revenue over five days; that is an estimate, not a company-reported audited figure.
The launch is a major result for a single-player release, though the saved evidence does not show how many players remain active after launch week.

scoreNotes.general: An unusually large launch for a single-player action game, backed by the studio’s reported sales figure and a separate analyst estimate.
scoreNotes.heat: GamesRadar reported four million copies sold and an 820,000-player Steam peak; Alinea Analytics estimated $223 million in combined Steam and PS5 revenue over five days.
scoreNotes.time: The four-million milestone was reported as a 72-hour result after the October 29 launch, placing it within the preceding seven days but outside the confirmed 24-hour window.
scoreNotes.ethos: The sales milestone is attributed to S-Game. The revenue figure is an analyst estimate, not a reported audited total, and the saved results do not establish ongoing retention.
